title: Upper Deck Cabin Runs Warm on Long Sectors — Request for Revised Temperature Control
abstract: Skyline International Airways asks for the cabin temperature control to be retuned after persistent warm-cabin complaints in the aft upper deck, which the crew currently manage by selecting the coldest position for the whole deck.

sections.request: The back of the upper deck runs warm and has done for years. On a night sector out of Singapore the crew will set the aft upper deck to the coldest position within the first hour and leave it there for the rest of the flight, which then makes the forward part of the same deck too cold and generates a second set of complaints. The crew tell us the selector does not seem to do very much once the cabin is full. We have had the trim air valves changed on two aircraft with no difference. Our cabin crew have started handing out extra blankets in the front of the upper deck as standard practice, which tells you the system is not doing what the crew ask of it.
sections.background: Cabin comfort complaints for the aft upper deck run at 3.4 per thousand passengers against 0.6 for the main deck. Temperature recordings taken by our engineering team on four sectors show a steady 3 to 4 degree difference between the front and the back of the upper deck once the cabin is above 80 per cent load. The trim air hardware tested serviceable on every occasion. Our own view is that this is a control law issue rather than a hardware issue.
sections.expected_outcome: Independent and effective temperature control of the forward and aft upper deck cabins at full passenger load, without the crew having to bias the whole deck to one extreme, and without any change to the cabin attendant panel that would need retraining.

type_data.business_justification: Cabin comfort complaints on the aft upper deck at 3.4 per thousand passengers, nearly six times the main deck rate, on the cabin the operator sells at the highest yield.
